newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T eases gently after Q1 figures.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T eases gently after Q1 figures.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc eased back in early trading after it reported first quarter profits in line with forecasts, dealers said.
B.A.T shares were down three pence, or 0.57 percent, to 521p by 0740 GMT in volume of 575,000 while the FTSE-100 index was 28.0 points, or 0.63 percent, higher at 4,461.2.
"The figures were perhaps slightly disappointing overall," a marketmaker at a British bank said.

British tobacco-to-insurance group B.A.T reported first quarter profits of 591 million stg. The company said pre-tax profit was hit by a 22 million stg provision for a factory closure and exchange rate movements.
Analysts had forecast first-quarter pre-tax profits of 544-610 million stg, after 590 million stg in 1996.
B.A.T said in a statement accompanying the results that the string of lawsuits it is facing in the U.S. will have no material impact on its finances.

B.A.T's U.S. subsidiary Brown & Williamson is facing a string of lawsuits, including 24 cases bought by state attorneys general seeking to recover Medicaid funds spent helping patients with tobacco-related illnesses.
Elsewhere in the British tobacco sector, Imperial Tobacco Group Plc was off 1p at 407p with dealers saying there was stock in the market.
Overnight, New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said he backed the City Council's idea of banning tobacco advertisements near schools.

Earlier the council said it planned to unveil on Wednesday a bill that would restrict advertising and promotion of tobacco products within 1,000 feet of schools and other places where children gather.
New York was one of the first U.S. cities to restrict smoking in restaurants, workplaces and other public areas.
